give the sack = to fire someone (informal British)
look for a job = to try to find paid work
get hired = to be given a job
lose your job = to stop having paid work, often because the company no longer needs you
career = the series of jobs you do in your working life
profession = a job that needs special training, such as teaching or law
manual work = work done with your hands and body, not only at a desk
white-collar = connected with office work rather than physical work
blue-collar = connected with factory or practical skilled work
customer service = helping people who buy from a company
deal with = to take action about a person or problem at work
be in charge of = to have responsibility for people or a task
work overtime = to work extra hours after normal time
commute = to travel regularly between home and work
rush hour = the busy time when many people travel to or from work
work-life balance = a fair division of time between job and private life
stress at work = worry caused by your job
teamwork = working well with other people to finish a job
meeting = a time when people at work discuss things together
contract = a written agreement about your job and pay
